chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Al Hibbler and Ozzie Bailey
summary: Hibbler's affliction made it hard to keep up; Brown did not know Bailey.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, there again, Al with his affliction, it was hard for him to keep up, and they would have really had to hire another person just to take care of Al, which he was such a good voice, that when he did leave or when he changed, he was able to hire another -- someone to take care of him. He did quite well. So I really don't know what happens in those cases. He's still in Teaneck, New Jersey, I hear. In fact, he came to L. A. not long ago for a stint at a little off club, but it wasn't too good, I hear.
This was when he played the Parisian a while back?
That's the last place I can remember him playing in.
Unless he's played somewhere else. (Unintelligible). Ozzie Bailey?
No. No, he was while I was out.
